baseline.worktree: Already contained uncommitted passes 09-11; not clean-release acceptance
baseline.publication: No version change, commit, tag, push or deployment.

scope.meaning: HTTP event retention/overflow settings through owner admission, persistence barrier, policy/trim transaction and cache publication; history, unread and DropNew boundaries.
scope.boundaries: Actual Axum handlers with synthetic sessions and EventBus injected with private Unix-socket PostgreSQL 16.15; DATABASE_URL unset.
excluded: new routes/access tiers/Event/database schema/SDK signature or frontend product-source changes

findings.summary: Settings reads returned 200 during missing-table failure, prior fallback or corrupt policy instead of unavailable.
findings.fix: Fresh fallible HTTP reads from configured storage, try_get decoding and stored policy/limit validation. Only absent rows are valid defaults. Generic no-store 503 on failure, bounded waiting, no runtime-cache publication or persistence-disable latch.

findings.summary: Failed persistence barriers could acknowledge a volatile settings save; definite SQL errors were client 400 errors and code forwarded raw storage text.
findings.fix: HTTP-specific confirmed save rejects unavailable configured storage, prior fallback and failed barriers; policy plus trim commit atomically before shared cache publication. Definite query failures preserve memory and remain retryable; generic no-store 503 instead of raw SQL.

findings.summary: Save blocked on local publication exceeded a 12-second test bound; successful settings GET lacked no-store.
findings.fix: Reuse ten-second cooperative service wait with owner admission retained by dispatched SQL workers after caller cancellation/expiry. Unconfirmed is not rollback. Success and handler errors are private JSON; body failures retain 400/413/415/422.

first_http_fix.note: Before final expanded body-limit/content-type and auth/Origin assertions.

tdd.after_red_guards: Four additional SQL cases, two ordinary service cases and HTTP body/auth guards were added after reproducing initial failures. Tests stop on their first failing assertion; corrupt-type/limit and repaired branches are protective coverage, not separately observed pre-fix failures.

operational_diagnostic.meaning: First gate launch used an unquoted PATH containing spaces, so env failed before checks ran. Corrected launch passed; not a product defect.

quality_gate.compatibility: OpenAPI/API/SDK generation and surface checks passed at unchanged version 0.4.0; 64 paths, 68 Engine operations, 63 SDK operations, 85 schemas
quality_gate.note: Tool/SSH/kernel-smoke checks are isolated fixtures, not privileged deployment acceptance.

post_documentation_preflight.meaning: Final bilingual report/course mirrors and common checks, with tested runtime sources unchanged.

event_postgres.command: env -u DATABASE_URL CYANREX_DB_FALLBACK=true CYANREX_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<explicit disposable private socket URL> cargo test --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --locked --lib services::event_bus::tests -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
event_postgres.note: Includes admitted save cancellation, a post-commit cache-publication timeout, a blocked-before-commit transaction, retryable reads, atomic SQL errors, fresh-bus reload and read flags/DropNew capacity.

contract_ci.note: 51 exact ordering-job selections plus the separately selected deletion cover 52 event SQL cases; nonempty selection guards retained.

preservation.note: Original inventory and historical pass 01-11 documents/reports/logs/mirrors remain byte-identical, including uncommitted passes 09-11.

limitations: Unconfirmed is not rollback: dispatched SQL or cache publication may finish after caller timeout/cancellation or response loss. Verify state before explicit retry; no automatic retries.
The blocked-before-commit test observes rollback in that fixture; it is not a lost-commit or general timeout-rollback guarantee.
Ten seconds bounds cooperative service waiting, not auth/body extraction/serialization, CPU stalls or the whole admitted worker lifetime.
Definite query errors remain retryable; prior write/barrier/storage failures can latch fallback. Repair/restart does not reconcile volatile events.
Fresh HTTP settings reads do not update runtime policy caches or coordinate external writers. Legacy settings/publication helpers retain cached best-effort fallback.
Explicit memory-only HTTP success is volatile; owner ordering only spans one EventBus and its clones. No multi-Engine coordination, crash recovery, shutdown drain or durable replay.
Frontend product source unchanged; no new live browser-to-Engine acceptance.
